newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dealers reaction mixed to Thyssen, Krupp news.
newsitem.headline: Dealers reaction mixed to Thyssen, Krupp news.

text.p: German share dealers said on Monday they were waiting until share trade on Tuesday to see the full effect of the announcement by engineering groups Thyssen and Krupp that Krupp had withdrawn the takeover bid.

Shares in the two firms were among the biggest gainers in afternoon trade with Krupp-Hoesch ending up 17.50 marks, or 5.48 percent, at 337 marks, and Thyssen ending the day up 20 marks, or 5.12 percent, at 410.50 marks.

"Logically the Thyssen share price should fall through 400 marks tomorrow, but if they go ahead with some kind of joint venture and include a restructuring, then the market will probably like that," a trader said.
In a joint statement which came after the end of trade, Krupp and Thyssen said that Krupp had withdrawn the takeover bid, and that talks over the steel merger were going well.
The two groups said they would explore cooperation outside the steel area and that Krupp planned no further takeover bid in future.
Krupp said that its decision to drop a hostile takeover bid did not herald a friendly merger, but there was scope for joint ventures outside the steel production area.
"This does not mean there will be a merger between the two groups," a Krupp spokesman said.
Thyssen would take over executive control of the steel joint venture with Krupp.

"This could be a better outcome. Krupp said that they had the cash to take over Thyssen but I still think they would have been stretched financially to do it. This is a better solution all round," the trader said.
"The market would probably go for a quasi-restructuring," he said.
Another trader was less optimistic and said that there had been talk of Thyssen shares trading at 390 marks in unofficial trade.
"I believe the Thyssen share price will fall tomorrow, but the fundamental positive effect of a fusion of their respective steel divisions will be seen as positive," said a trader.
Thyssen rose over the day on reports it was planning to tell shareholders its shares have the potential to reach a price of around 550 marks.
Last week Krupp announced a takeover bid for the larger Thyssen. Since then Thyssen agreed to discuss a joint steel company. Krupp had said it planned to reinstate the offer should the talks fail.
